best_narrative.headline: Zocdoc: Telehealth Rivals Mobilize Federal Lobbying on Prescription Economics
best_narrative.body: Zocdoc operates a healthcare directory and marketplace connecting patients to telehealth providers, creating material exposure to state medical advertising, consumer protection, and anti-kickback regulation across New York, California, and Texas. Four competing telehealth operators filed federal lobbying disclosures in May 2026 targeting prescription economics and access policy, signaling coordinated industry advocacy on reimbursement, supply chain, and prescriber-patient matching rules. State-level enforcement activity on telehealth advertising and fee arrangements typically follows federal attention to these categories. Zocdoc's government affairs team should monitor whether these federal filings translate to state rule proposals that could affect provider contracting, patient attribution, or marketplace commission structures.

[Rep Name]

Four major competitors just filed coordinated federal lobbying on prescription economics in May, which typically signals incoming state rule proposals. Let's grab 10 minutes so I can show you what the federal filings say about state rule risk and help your compliance leadership stay ahead of it.

best_narrative.headline: Spring Health: Competitor Federal Lobbying Escalates Telehealth Regulatory Pressure
best_narrative.body: Spring Health operates as a pure-play mental health platform dependent on state behavioral health licensing reciprocity and employer plan contracting, creating material exposure when regulatory momentum shifts. Two competitors filed federal lobbying disclosures on telehealth topics in April 2026, signaling industry mobilization around asynchronous prescribing standards and interstate licensing frameworks. Operators in this segment commonly face tightening state-level requirements around prescriber supervision, credential verification, and Medicaid reimbursement tiering. New York, California, and Florida account for the highest concentration of Spring Health's licensing and plan-relationship dependencies.
